sourceContext.originPage: WKND magazine article detail page (magazine-article template)

contentPattern.structure: single [author image] | [name (heading) + role/occupations + 3 social links] row

suitableFor: single-person profile rows shown at the end of an article
compact horizontal profile: small round photo + name + role + social links
notSuitableFor: team / staff / contributor GRIDS of multiple centered cards (use cards-profile)
article / product / adventure card grids (use the plain 'cards' block)

notes: New variant derived from the project-local 'cards-profile' block, which already carries the correct people-profile content model and doc-project adaptations (imports only createOptimizedPicture from aem.js; no moveInstrumentation). A DISTINCT name (cards-author) is used instead of reusing cards-profile because, although the CONTENT MODEL is identical (row = [image] | [name + role + social links]), the VISUAL LAYOUT differs significantly: cards-profile renders a responsive GRID of centered, circular-photo team cards (About Us contributors/guides, spacious, large images, 2-4 columns), whereas cards-author renders a SINGLE horizontal byline row (left-aligned small round photo + name/role stacked, social icons inline, divided from the article body by an hr). Similarity scoring against cards-profile metadata was ~30% (purpose team vs author-bio, density spacious vs compact, imagePattern large vs small), well below the 80% reuse threshold. Content model: row 1 = block name; each subsequent row = 2 cells [author image] | [name (heading) + role paragraph + social links]. Decoration converts rows to <ul><li>, sets the single-picture cell to .cards-author-card-image and the text cell to .cards-author-card-body, tags the first non-link paragraph as .cards-author-card-role, and gathers the social <a> elements into a .cards-author-social row (labels Facebook/Twitter/Instagram; placeholder hrefs preserved). The preceding hr separator from the source is authored as default content in the section, not part of the block. Reused across all 4 magazine-article pages in the group.
